newsitem.title: FRANCE: French deputy backs jobs over low inflation.
newsitem.headline: French deputy backs jobs over low inflation.

text.p: French deputy Pierre Mazeaud, a member of President Jacques Chirac's conservative Gaullist RPR party, urged the government on Sunday to be more tolerant of inflation and a weaker franc if it would create jobs.

"I consider jobs to be the main problem in our country. For that, we must boost consumption ... I am among those who believe that a bit of inflation would not be bad if it made money cheaper and convinced people to begin consuming again," he said.
"I am one of those who would favour a change," he said in an interview on French television TF 1.
"That said, (Prime Minister Alain) Juppe's policies are good and he is a great man," Mazeaud added.
France is suffering from near-record 12.7 percent unemployment but the government has kept down public deficits and spending to help Paris qualify for European monetary union.
